spike_swarm_sim.utils.initializers module¶

class spike_swarm_sim.utils.initializers.Initializer(num_points, engine='3D', variable='position')[source]¶

Bases: object

Base class of the entity initializers. Initializers allow the automatic initialization of either the positions or orientations of world objects as a group. For example it allows to sample positions uniformly within a square without physical overlapping or sample the 2D coordinates of robots in a swarm as a 2D spatial random graph (assuring swarm compactness). If created correctly within the world class, the __call__ method of the initializer is executed every time that the world/environment is reset. This base class should not be instantiated directly and every initializer should inherit from it.

Once instantiated, it is executed using the __call__ method, that returns a list of sampled positions or orientations.

Parameters:
  • num_points (int) – number of points to sample in the initialization.
  • engine (str) – physics and render engine used (currently it can be either 2D or 3D)
  • variable (str) – entity variable to be initialized (either ‘positions’ or ‘orientations’)
class spike_swarm_sim.utils.initializers.FixedInitializer(*args, fixed_values=None, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: spike_swarm_sim.utils.initializers.Initializer

Initializer class that initializes the positions or orientations always at the given fixed values.

Reference Name: fixed.

Parameters:
  • num_points (int) – number of points to sample in the initialization.
  • engine (str) – physics and render engine used (currently it can be either 2D or 3D)
  • variable (str) – entity variable to be initialized (either ‘positions’ or ‘orientations’)
  • fixed_values (list) – list of the fixed value of the variable to be initialized for each entity in the group. The length of the list must equal the num_points arg.
class spike_swarm_sim.utils.initializers.FixedRandomInitializer(*args, possible_values=None, replacement=True, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: spike_swarm_sim.utils.initializers.Initializer

Initializer class that initializes the positions or orientations randomly from a list of fixed possible values. Each defined value has the same probability to be chosen and the sampling can be with or without replacement (it is advised to sample with replacement).

Reference Name: fixed_random.

Parameters:
  • num_points (int) – number of points to sample in the initialization.
  • engine (str) – physics and render engine used (currently it can be either 2D or 3D)
  • variable (str) – entity variable to be initialized (either ‘positions’ or ‘orientations’)
  • possible_values (list) – list of the possible values to be sampled with equal prob.
  • replacement (bool) – whether to sample with replacement or not.
class spike_swarm_sim.utils.initializers.RandomUniformInitializer(*args, low=[-2, -2], high=[2, 2], size=2, min_dist=1.0, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: spike_swarm_sim.utils.initializers.Initializer

Initializer class that initializes the positions randomly within a defined rectangular area (positions) or within a segment (orientations).

  1. Sampling positions: If sampling from a rectangle, the area is specified using the arguments low and high, which the are bottom left and top right rectangle vertices. The coordinates are sampled from the rectangle randomly according to an uniform dist. If sampling positions, potential overlapping between objects is avoided using the min_dist attribute.
  2. Sampling orientations: Samples the orientations from a uniform distribution \(\mathcal{U}(low, high)\). Normally, it is used as \(\mathcal{U}(0, 2\pi)\).

Reference Name: random_uniform.

Parameters:
  • num_points (int) – number of points to sample in the initialization.
  • engine (str) – physics and render engine used (currently it can be either 2D or 3D)
  • variable (str) – entity variable to be initialized (either ‘positions’ or ‘orientations’)
  • low (list) – low 2D or 1D coordinates of the rectangle or segment used to uniformly sample. If sampling orientations then the type of the arg is float instead of list.
  • high (list) – high 2D or 1D coordinates of the rectangle or segment used to uniformly sample. If sampling orientations then the type of the arg is float instead of list.
  • size (int) – dim. of the hyperrectangle used to sample.
  • min_dist (float) – minimum distance between any pair of sampled points.
class spike_swarm_sim.utils.initializers.RandomCircleInitializer(*args, center=[0, 0], radius=1.0, min_dist=0.6, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: spike_swarm_sim.utils.initializers.Initializer

Class for randomly initializing objects positions within a circle area. Each point within the area has the same probability (uniform dist.) and overlapping objects are avoided. For that, a minimum distance between points is defined.

It uniformly samples a random angle and radius and computes the cartesian position corresponding to the sampled polar coordinates.

Reference Name: random_circle.

Parameters:
  • num_points (int) – number of points to sample in the initialization.
  • engine (str) – physics and render engine used (currently it can be either 2D or 3D)
  • variable (str) – entity variable to be initialized (either ‘positions’ or ‘orientations’)
  • radius (float) – maximum radius to be sampled.
  • center (list) – center of the circle where points are sampled.
  • min_dist (float) – minimum distance between any pair of sampled points.

spike_swarm_sim.utils.activations module¶

spike_swarm_sim.utils.activations.heaviside(x)[source]¶

Applies a Heaviside activation function.

\[\mathcal{H}(x) = \left\{\begin{array}{ccc} 1, & \text{ if } & x >=0 \\ 0, & \text{ if } & x < 0 \\ \end{array}\right.\]
Parameters:x (np.ndarray) – input vector to which the activation is applied.
Returns:numpy array with the element-wise transformed vector.
spike_swarm_sim.utils.activations.relu(x)[source]¶

Applies a ReLU () activation function to the input vector.

\[\mathrm{relu}(x) = \left\{egin{array}{ccc} x, & ext{ if } & x >=0 \ 0, & ext{ if } & x < 0 \ \end{array}

ight.]

param np.ndarray x:
 input vector to which the activation is applied.
returns:numpy array with the element-wise transformed vector.
spike_swarm_sim.utils.activations.sigmoid(x)[source]¶

Applies a sigmoid activation function to the input vector.

\[\sigma(x) = \dfrac{1}{1 + e^{-x}}\]
Parameters:x (np.ndarray) – input vector to which the activation is applied.
Returns:numpy array with the element-wise transformed vector.
spike_swarm_sim.utils.activations.tanh(x)[source]¶

Applies a hyperbolic tangent activation function to the input vector.

\[\mathrm{tanh}(x) = \dfrac{e^{2x} - 1}{e^{2x} + 1}\]
Parameters:x (np.ndarray) – input vector to which the activation is applied.
Returns:numpy array with the element-wise transformed vector.
spike_swarm_sim.utils.activations.softmax(x, tau=1)[source]¶

Applies a softmax activation function to the input vector.

\[\mathrm{softmax}(x)_j = \dfrac{e^{\mathbf{x}_j/\tau}}{\displaystyle \sum_{ i} e^{x_i / \tau} }\]
Parameters:x (np.ndarray) – input vector to which the activation is applied.
Returns:numpy array with the element-wise transformed vector.
